messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test asserts:
  - In DOMModelTest.testAxisAttribute(), the XPath "vendor/product/price:amount/@*" is evaluated and expected to iterate over all attributes of the element price:amount, returning a set of values {"10%", "20%"}.
  - The comment notes DOM returns attributes sorted by name (hence comparing as a set). The key is that "@*" should include all attributes regardless of namespace or prefix.

- How attribute selection is implemented:
  - DOMAttributeIterator(NodePointer parent, QName name) constructs the attribute list.
    - If the QName’s local name is "*", it enumerates all attributes and filters them through testAttr(Attr) (lines 56–63).
  - testAttr(Attr attr) performs the matching logic (lines 68–98):
    - It skips xmlns attributes (lines 72–78).
    - It then checks if the test local name equals "*" or matches the attribute’s local name (line 81).
    - It retrieves the test prefix via name.getPrefix() (line 82).
    - Current logic:
      - If equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix) then return true (lines 84–86).
      - Else, it compares namespace URIs: it computes testNS only if testPrefix != null; nodeNS only if nodePrefix != null; then returns equalStrings(testNS, nodeNS) (lines 87–95).

- Why "@*" fails to match namespaced attributes:
  - For the expression "@*":
    - QName.getName() is "*" and QName.getPrefix() is null (no prefix specified).
    - testAttr sees testLocalName="*" (passes line 81).
    - testPrefix is null (line 82).
    - equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix) is false when the attribute has a prefix (nodePrefix != null), so the quick return is not taken (line 84).
    - testNS remains null because testPrefix == null (lines 87–90).
    - nodeNS is set to the attribute’s namespace URI when nodePrefix != null (lines 91–94).
    - equalStrings(testNS, nodeNS) compares null against a real namespace URI and returns false (line 95).
    - Result: any namespaced (prefixed) attribute is incorrectly filtered out by testAttr for "@*".
  - This exactly matches the bug report: xml/@* returns null (or misses prefixed attributes), while @x:* works because testPrefix is "x", causing either:
    - equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix) to succeed immediately when prefixes match; or
    - namespace comparison to succeed when testNS equals nodeNS.

- How this triggers the test failure:
  - In "vendor/product/price:amount/@*", the iterator is built with name="*", prefix=null.
  - The element price:amount has attributes, at least some of which are in a namespace (prefixed).
  - During enumeration, testAttr rejects prefixed attributes due to the null testPrefix logic above, so fewer (or no) attributes are returned.
  - The test expects both "10%" and "20%", but the iterator does not include namespaced attributes, causing the assertion to fail.

- Root cause:
  - DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr(Attr) treats a null test prefix as if it had to match the attribute’s namespace (by comparing null testNS against the attribute’s non-null nodeNS). For the wildcard "@*", a null test prefix should mean “any prefix/namespace,” not “must match a null namespace.”
  - The suggested fix in the bug report aligns with this: change the condition to accept any nodePrefix when testPrefix is null.

In summary, the filtering logic in DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr fails to include namespaced attributes when the attribute axis uses a wildcard without a prefix (e.g., "@*"), leading directly to the test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
